message.content:
Below you’ll find two ways to spin‑up a **Google Compute Engine** VM that has:

| Item | Details |
|------|---------|
| OS   | Ubuntu 20.04 LTS (`ubuntu-os-cloud/ubuntu-2004-focal-v20231102`) |
| GPU  | NVIDIA® RTX A6000 (24 GB) – one per instance |
| Machine type | Custom or predefined (e.g., `nvidia-tesla-a100`, but we’ll show custom so you can pick CPU/RAM that fits your workload) |

> ⚠️ *Note:*  
> • You must have the **GPU quota** enabled for the zone where you launch the instance.  
> • Make sure the **NVIDIA driver package** is installed after boot (the script below does that automatically).

---

### Option 1 – Using the `gcloud` CLI  

```bash
PROJECT_ID="your-project-id"
ZONE="us-central1-b"          # choose a zone that supports RTX A6000
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-demo"

# Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
    --project="$PROJECT_ID" \
    --zone="$ZONE" \
    --machine-type=n1-standard-8 \            # 8 vCPU + 30 GB RAM (adjust)
    --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1 \
    --maintenance-policy=MIGRATE \
    --provisioning-model=CUSTOM \
    --boot-disk-size=50GB \
    --boot-disk-type=pd-balanced \
    --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
    --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
    --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \
    --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \
    --tags=http-server,https-server
```

#### `startup.sh` – install drivers & enable CUDA

Create a small shell script named `startup.sh` in the same directory:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
set -euxo pipefail

# Update packages
apt-get update && apt-get upgrade -y

# Install NVIDIA driver (Ubuntu 20.04 includes 470+ kernel modules)
add-apt-repository ppa:graphics-drivers/ppa -y
apt-get update
DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535

# Reboot required for driver init
reboot
```

*If you prefer CUDA Toolkit installation, add those steps after reboot.*

After running the above `gcloud` command, the VM boots, runs `startup.sh`, installs the NVIDIA driver, reboots, and then you’re ready to SSH into the instance and start training!

---

### Option 2 – Direct REST API Call (JSON)

Use the following JSON body against the endpoint:
```
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/<PROJECT>/zones/<ZONE>/instances
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer <ACCESS_TOKEN>
```

Replace `<PROJECT>` and `<ZONE>` appropriately.

```json
{
  "name": "<instance-name>",
  "description": "Instance with RTX A6000 GPU",
  "machineType": "projects/<PROJECT>/zones/<ZONE>/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",

  "disks": [
    {
      "deviceName": "bootdisk",
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 50,
        "diskType": "pd-balanced"
      }
    }
  ],

  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "networkTier": "PREMIUM",
      "accessConfigs": [{ "kind":"compute#accessConfig","name":"External NAT","type":"ONE_TO_ONE_NAT"}]
    }
  ],

  "guestAccelerators": [
    { 
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/<PROJECT>/zones/<ZONE>/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000"
    }
  ],

  "serviceAccounts": [{
     "email":"default",
     "scopes":["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
  }],

  "scheduling": {"preemptible": false},

  "labels":{"purpose":"ml-training"},
  "metadata":{
    "items":[{"key":"startup-script","value":"\u0027#!/usr/bin/env bash\nsudo apt-get update\nsudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535\n\u0027"}
    ]
  },

  "reservationAffinity":{"consumeReservationType":"ANY_RESERVATION"}
}
```

Send the request via curl, Postman, or any SDK that handles OAuth scopes.

---

### Quick Checklist Before Launch

| ✅ | Task |
|----|------|
| ✔︎ Enable **GPUs** in the target zone (`gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com`). |
| ✔︎ Verify **quota** for `nvidia-tesla-a6000`. |
| ✔︎ Ensure **billing** is active for the project. |
| ✔︎ Add **firewall rules** if you plan to expose ports (HTTP/S). |
| ✔︎ After first boot, run `nvidia-smi` to confirm driver/GPU visibility. |

That’s all! Once the instance comes online, just SSH in and you’ll see `/dev/nvidia0` available along with the full CUDA stack. Happy training!
